name: Tiered Roof
summary: Three pitched roof tiers rise above an open prayer hall beside a crescent-topped minaret.
why: The stacked roof planes reference a mosque tradition beyond the familiar dome. Generous spaces between the tiers keep the triangular silhouette airy, while the pointed entrance and minaret establish the place of prayer.
risk: Tiered roofs may first suggest a pavilion to viewers unfamiliar with this mosque tradition; the minaret and crescent provide the Islamic cue. This is an invented interpretation, not an exact historical building.
reasonToChoose: A mosque with a less expected architectural silhouette feels right.
